existing_expressibility.named_relation_signature: Source {:f}((RELATION)){:r} Target expresses the specific Relation, directional endpoints and independent allowed counts when both counts are supplied. A signature describes admitted edges; it does not create every possible edge.
existing_expressibility.inverse: HAS_INVERSE records the derived reverse; reverse endpoint sets and counts swap. Do not create separately authored inverse facts.
existing_expressibility.inheritance: The selected MODEL resolves inherited and explicitly overridden rules. Existing Rule states absent effective-whitelist Relations are forbidden, and unresolved whitelist grants nothing.
existing_expressibility.limitation: A positive signature does not by itself document whether its list is complete. CFEL documentation does not define a general wildcard Relation-name selector, closed-set literal, or how to distinguish a complete whitelist signature set from ordinary Relation constraints. `Event Record.Relations.*[Relation//]` constrains child Property names, not the effective graph Relation whitelist.

minimal_candidate.decision_needed: Define which existing unguarded named Relation endpoint/count signatures in a Node Declaration are whitelist entries, then treat their MODEL-resolved inherited/local set as closed; apply explicit MODEL overrides before closure. No new relation-selection syntax is required if this convention is accepted.
requirements: A complete entry must provide the applicable endpoint selectors, direction and both directional counts; omitted counts remain undefined, not zero or 0+.
A zero-count constraint is a prohibition, not a positive entry. Conditional or nested Relation references are constraints, not automatically unconditional whitelist grants.
The selected MODEL determines applicable inherited entries and explicit local replacements; no ancestor restatement and no automatic permission union from an unresolved base.
Classify authored direct facts and derived inverse views without requiring the inverse to be authored. A zero-count or closed whitelist must not accidentally prohibit an allowed derived view.
Name and close the effective set in each applicable Declaration whether its Claim contains prose or is formal-only. Unresolved endpoint, inherited entry or count means incomplete, never default-any.
A declared endpoint signature permits matching links and does not create cross-product facts.
minimal_candidate.unresolved: Existing CFEL does not say whether top-level signatures carry whitelist membership or provide an explicit complete-list delimiter. If ordinary signature expressions can be incomplete drafts or conditional uses, automatic closure risks forbidding valid edges. This proposal is a semantic convention and needs explicit approval.

source_backed_examples.what_it_establishes: A selected outgoing CONTAINS constraint for Event Records; the converse count and all inherited or other local Relation permissions are not specified by this expression.
source_backed_examples.not_a_claim: It is not a complete whitelist and does not authorize all Event Record relations.

source_backed_examples.what_it_establishes: One outgoing direct containment to Journal; reverse count and other permissions need their own effective entries. The event-author signature and Actor reference do not alone establish a complete local whitelist.
source_backed_examples.not_a_claim: Do not assign invented counts to IS_EVENT_AUTHOR_OF or assume all relation names from the record carrier group are graph permissions.

source_backed_examples.what_it_establishes: The Relation Definition specifies allowed Property-to-Node endpoints, with one bearer stated in its Claim and Node classification rules. It is not automatically each Property Declaration’s complete whitelist.
source_backed_examples.not_a_claim: Do not equate Property bearer syntax or Node.Relations.* with a generic dynamic Relation selector.

single_blocking_question.question: Should each Node Declaration’s top-level CFEL Relation signatures, after selected-MODEL inheritance and explicit overrides, be the complete closed whitelist for that Node, with any needed conditional, zero-count and derived-inverse cases distinguished by rule?
single_blocking_question.option_a: Yes: specify the signature-to-whitelist interpretation and completeness test in the reusable Rule; resolve missing counts and endpoints before adoption.
single_blocking_question.option_b: No: decide an explicit general whitelist-set notation and its inheritance/override semantics before asserting formal completeness.
single_blocking_question.recommended: Option A if ordinary endpoint signatures can be unambiguously classified as whitelist entries; otherwise Option B. Neither is already established as CFEL syntax.

limits: No draft edits, source adoption, parser implementation, instance audit or inferred default-all permissions.
